# temps_cluster_network (Resource)

Address pool and overlay network the nodes of the cluster give workloads. Temps refuses a change while `can_change` is false (workloads use the current pool); `change_blocked_by` says why.

Destroying the resource leaves the network as it is; it only stops managing it.

Import with `cluster_network`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `settings:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_cluster_network" "this" {
  compute_pool_cidr = "10.200.0.0/16"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `compute_pool_cidr` (String) CIDR workload subnets are taken from.

### Optional

- `overlay_network_name` (String) Name of the overlay network.
- `subnet_prefix_len` (Number) Prefix length of each node's subnet.

### Read-Only

- `can_change` (Boolean) Whether the pool can be changed now.
- `change_blocked_by` (List of String) What prevents a change.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `cluster_network`.
- `mesh_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the WireGuard mesh is on.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Singleton: the import ID is the resource type without the prefix.
terraform import temps_cluster_network.this cluster_network
```
